_about: Knowledge base of education technology tools and low-resource teaching strategies. Grounds the Auditor (which proposes tools) and the FAQ agent (which explains them). Each entry notes connectivity and device requirements so suggestions stay realistic for rural classrooms.

tools.name: Plickers
tools.what: A free assessment tool where each student holds a printed paper card (a QR-like code). The teacher scans the whole class with ONE phone camera; students rotate their card to choose A/B/C/D. No student devices or internet needed during scanning.
tools.needs_internet: Only to set up questions beforehand and to view saved reports. The in-class scan works offline once the question set is loaded.
tools.devices_required: 1 teacher device (phone/tablet) + printed cards (free to print).
how_to_use: Create a free account and build a question set at home or wherever there is internet.
Print one Plickers card per student (reusable, laminate if possible).
In class, display or read the question; students raise their card oriented to their answer.
Open the Plickers app and pan the camera across the room to capture every answer at once.
Review instant class results; save for reports later when back online.
tools.offline_alternative: A/B/C/D coloured paper cards or fingers (1-4) for instant voting without any device.

tools.name: Kahoot!
tools.what: A live multiplayer quiz game projected on a screen; students answer on their own devices.
tools.needs_internet: Yes, for every player in classic mode.
tools.devices_required: Teacher device + projector + one device per student or per group.
how_to_use: Create or pick a quiz.
Host it; a game PIN appears on the shared screen.
Students join with the PIN on their devices and answer against the clock.
tools.offline_alternative: Run it as a team game: project questions, teams huddle and hold up an answer card. Or use 'Paper Kahoot' with corner-of-the-room voting.

tools.name: Google Classroom
tools.what: A hub to post materials, assignments and feedback.
tools.needs_internet: Yes to sync, but content can be downloaded for offline reading on Android.
tools.devices_required: Any device with a browser or the app.
how_to_use: Create a class and share the join code.
Post materials and assignments.
Students submit work; teacher grades and comments.
tools.offline_alternative: Distribute the same materials on a USB drive or printed packet; collect work on paper.

tools.name: Quizizz
tools.what: Quizzes students complete at their own pace; supports paper mode.
tools.needs_internet: Yes for live mode; Paper Mode needs internet only on the teacher device.
tools.devices_required: Teacher device + printed answer cards (Paper Mode) OR student devices.
how_to_use: Pick or build a quiz.
Use Paper Mode: print cards, scan answers with the teacher device, like Plickers.
tools.offline_alternative: Printed worksheet with self-check answer key.

tools.name: PhET Simulations
tools.what: Free interactive simulations (e.g. circuits, forces, fractions) from the University of Colorado.
tools.needs_internet: No — simulations can be DOWNLOADED and run offline.
tools.devices_required: 1 device + projector is enough for a whole-class demo.
how_to_use: Download the relevant simulation while online.
Project it and manipulate variables as a class, or let groups take turns on one device.
Pair with a guided worksheet.
tools.offline_alternative: Hands-on physical demonstration or a teacher-drawn animation on the board.

tools.name: Kolibri
tools.what: An open-source offline platform (by Learning Equality) that serves Khan Academy and other content from a local device with no internet.
tools.needs_internet: Only once, to load the content library; then fully offline over a local hotspot.
tools.devices_required: 1 server device (laptop/Raspberry Pi) + client devices on a local network.
how_to_use: Install Kolibri and import content channels while online.
Run it as a local server; students connect over the device's hotspot/LAN.
Track progress locally; sync later if/when online.
tools.offline_alternative: Pre-downloaded videos played from a USB drive.

tools.name: Canva for Education
tools.what: Free design tool for posters, infographics and slides.
tools.needs_internet: Yes to create; exports (PDF/PNG) can be used offline once downloaded.
tools.devices_required: Teacher device; outputs can be printed.
how_to_use: Design a visual aid online.
Export and print, or display offline.

no_internet: Pre-download everything (videos, simulations, quizzes) while you have access elsewhere.
Use offline-first platforms like Kolibri served over a local hotspot.
Carry content on a USB drive; play from the teacher device through a projector/TV.
limited_connectivity: Use tools that sync opportunistically (Google Classroom offline, Quizizz Paper Mode).
one_device_only: Use the single device as a 'station' or a whole-class projection hub.
Tools where ONE camera scans the whole class: Plickers, Quizizz Paper Mode.
Rotate small groups through the device while others do unplugged tasks.
one_screen: Whole-class interactive demos: project a simulation and let students predict-observe-explain.
Think-Pair-Share around a single projected prompt.
limited_devices: Group-based rotation; pair stronger and weaker students.
Jigsaw method so each group masters one part using the shared device.
no_electricity: Use solar/power-bank-charged tablets for short bursts.
Printed manipulatives and unplugged coding activities (e.g. CS Unplugged).
